PROMPT 

Make "Plush Pigeon" (Material Studies No. 031) on the Plush Penguin WebGPU engine: XPBD soft-body lattice, shell fur, cloth wings, posture-driven gait, tools Hand / Finger / Comb.

The toy: a round, well-fed rock dove of soft grey minky.
- Shape: one SDF with a round body, a proud chest, a neck rising into a teal domed head, a flat tail with a dark band, and two pink felt feet with three toes forward and one behind.
- Neck ring: iridescent, green above and violet below, dipping lower over the chest.
- Face: glossy bead eyes with an orange ring; a small dark felt beak with a pale cere.
- Wings: two stuffed cloth wings sewn at the shoulders, folded down and back along the sides, each with two charcoal bars and a darker tip.
- Fur length: shorter on the head and neck ring, cropped to felt on the feet.

Life:
- Strut: a waddle in which neck-cell shear muscles bob the head with every step. Keep the bend normal orthogonal to the neck axis, or the shear pushes the whole body.
- Coo: the chest cells swell, the head bows twice, and a synthesized three-note rolling "croo" plays.
- Flap: wing flaps with hops and a feather-flutter sound.
- Topple, then get back up.
- Finger: struts over to a held finger; a boop on the beak makes it coo; it sometimes coos when idle.

Palettes: Blue bar, Ash red, Snow.
Readouts: mass, volume, steps, coos.
Responsive layout.

eu mandei um audio e ele transcrever, mas aqui ta o prompt q ele mesmo fez pra editar 

Edit my talking-head video into a polished YouTube video with explanatory motion graphics.

INPUT
- Raw video: <path/to/raw.mp4>. Speech is Portuguese; don't translate.
- Target: at most <6:30>. Style: premium, clean, editorial ("Anthropic/Apple level").
- End card: subscribe + follow me on X (<http://x.com/handle>) + "comment what you want to see next".
- Never cover my face. Never show where I live.

STACK
- Remotion (http://remotion.dev) for the composition, ffmpeg for cuts and encoding, Python for analysis.
- Transcribe with word timestamps using ElevenLabs Scribe. It has precise word boundaries and marks fillers like "hã"/"é".
- If you use Whisper instead: its word ends stretch over pauses, so refine every cut point with the audio energy.

1) PLAN THE CUT
- Make an indexed transcript (word index → text, start, end).
- Choose keep-ranges by word index. Remove fillers, false starts, repeated sentences and weak tangents until it fits the target.
- Put the strongest line (2–4 s) at the very start as a cold-open hook.

2) CUT, FRAME-ACCURATE AND IN SYNC
- Cut points:
  - Cut in the silence between words, never inside a word.
  - Keep ~50 ms before the first word and ~60 ms after the last word (~160 ms if it ends a sentence).
- Silences inside kept ranges:
  - Detect them with a 10 ms RMS envelope. A threshold around −38 dBFS worked here; measure your own noise floor first.
  - Shorten any pause over 0.32 s to 0.22 s (0.36 s after a sentence ends).
- Round every boundary to whole frames (30 fps) and merge touching segments.
- Video: ffmpeg split → trim(start_frame, end_frame) → concat, plus a light grade (hqdn3d, eq, colorbalance, unsharp) → intermediate at CRF 14.
- Audio: cut the same boundaries in numpy with 8 ms fades and no overlap. A/V stays in sync.
- QA: re-transcribe the cut and diff it against the intended text. Fix leaked fragments and clipped word starts, then repeat until clean.

3) FACE TRACK
- Detect the face every 0.2 s (Apple Vision or MediaPipe).
- Smooth with a moving average inside each cut segment, never across a jump cut.
- Use it to frame the camera and to place graphics on the side away from the face.

4) DESIGN SYSTEM
- One palette: dark warm stage #14120F, ivory "paper" #F1ECE2, one accent (clay #D97A4E).
- Fonts: Fraunces (serif display), Inter Tight (UI), JetBrains Mono (labels). Add subtle grain and soft glows.
- No gradient text, no neon.
- Camera layout modes, morphing between them in ~0.7 s (cubic in-out):
  - full frame;
  - split left/right: rounded camera card 856×936, face at 42% of its height, graphics on the other half;
  - PIP: 256 px circle over a full-screen paper sheet, for chapter moments.

5) BEAT SHEET (JSON)
- Give every sentence group a visual, cued to word start times in the cut timeline:
  - lower third (name/role);
  - big numbers with count-up;
  - lists that reveal on each spoken item;
  - SVG diagrams that draw on;
  - timeline, before→after, comparison cards, quotes;
  - arrows annotating objects in the room.
- Structure: cold open with kinetic captions → 1.5 s title card → content → end card (CTAs plus a portrait still).

6) BUILD IN REMOTION
- One composition, 1920×1080 at 30 fps. Put `<OffthreadVideo>` (muted) inside a container whose rect and transform come from the layout keyframes plus the face track.
- Each graphic is a `<Sequence>` component. Drive reveals with useCurrentFrame + interpolate/spring (opacity, translateY, blur).
- SVG draw-on: animate strokeDashoffset using the real path length.
- Jump cuts: alternate zoom 1.0 ↔ 1.075 around the face when the picture jumps. Add a 1–2% slow breathing zoom elsewhere and a punch-in on punchlines.
- Deterministic only: no Math.random.
- Check key frames with `npx remotion still`: face uncovered, no clipped text, nothing appearing before its cue.

7) SOUND
- Voice: highpass 80 Hz, light denoise, −2.5 dB at 280 Hz, +2 dB at 3.6 kHz, de-ess, 3:1 compressor.
- Music: royalty-free lo-fi (e.g. Mixkit). Change track per section with 4 s crossfades.
  - Duck 9–12 dB under the voice in the speech band, keeping the lows.
  - Louder only on the title and end cards.
- SFX: very subtle whooshes on layout changes, pops on reveals, ticks on counters.
- Master: two-pass loudnorm to −14 LUFS, true peak −1.5.

8) RENDER, VERIFY, DELIVER
- Encode: H.264 CRF 16, AAC 320k, BT.709, +faststart.
- Verify:
  - duration within the target, −14 LUFS;
  - no frozen stretch over 0.3 s;
  - a 40-frame contact sheet;
  - re-transcribe the final mix: at least 95% of words should match, so the music isn't masking the voice.
- Deliver the MP4, an .srt from the word timings (max 42 chars per line, 2 lines), and YouTube chapters (first at 0:00, each at least 10 s).

RULES
- Show numbers and claims exactly as I say them.
- Check names and spellings on the web before they go on screen.
- No invented stats or testimonials.
- Short, concrete on-screen copy with no AI clichés.
- Don't publish anything without my OK.

<inputs>
Ask me for: my product and the one request a user types into it, 6 to 8 photos for the result cards, a royalty-free song around 130 BPM with a clear drop (Mixkit, free for commercial use), and my brand mark for the end card. If I skip any, use the defaults: the food-ordering story below, food photos from Pexels (fire noodles, birria tacos, hot chicken, buffalo wings, smash burger, spicy ramen) and Mixkit "Cat Walk".
</inputs>

<direction>
A 15 second product launch film, 1920x1080 at 60fps, 2D only, one continuous take. Every scene is made out of the previous one: nothing fades, blurs or cuts. Objects change shape instead: text rises out of a mask line, buttons grow into pages, a color floods out of one object and later shrinks back into another. The camera makes one move per scene on eased keyframes and never zooms in and out back to back.
Look: warm white canvas #f5f5f2, black UI #0e0e10, lime accent #cdf24f, one orange #ff6a2a, a blue send button #2f6bff. An Apple Intelligence style iridescent glow (a rotating conic gradient of pink, orange, lime, cyan and violet, blurred) around the input. Real food photography on dark cards. Geist for UI, a serif for the product name on the end card.
Banned: crossfades, blur-ins, 3D, particles, camera moves that reverse direction, holds longer than 1s, anything that looks like a template.
</direction>

<structure>
130 BPM, 32 beats (14.8s). The song starts 12 beats before its drop.
Beats 0-6, ask: close on the glowing composer (about 3x zoom, a slow push). The request types on three fixed lines with a real keystroke rhythm: "I'm really hungry, I don't know / what I want but something / spicy, crispy and filling".
Beat 6, send: the send button presses, a lime fill ripples out of it and turns the message into the chat bubble, and one pull-back grows the phone around it (428x900 screen, 11px black bezel, 9:41 status bar).
Beats 6-12, think: the send button grows into an orange wok (a half-disc with a thin handle) that tosses 6 colored ingredients on beats 8, 9, 10 and 11, under a shimmering "Finding something for you…".
Beat 12, the drop: a lime circle floods out of the wok edge to edge in about 0.35s. Dark food cards (330x440, radius 28, photo on top, name, one-line description, price, rating) burst in from the center, and the strip slides three cards onto "Fire Noodles", which lifts with a "Best match" pill.
Beats 16-21, chat: the lime shrinks back into the user's bubble carrying its words, and the chosen card flies into its slot. "Found it. Fire Noodles from Wok & Fire, smoky, spicy and seriously filling." rises in, then "Want me to order it for you?" and two pills pop in: "Order now" (black) and "More options" (outline). The cursor clicks Order now → spinner → "✓ Ordered".
Beats 21-32, outro: the black button grows into the whole page. It stays a pill until it reaches the edges while the camera pushes into it, and its label grows to headline size, then slides out. "You were craving noodles." then "Now it's on the way." rise word by word (92px, white on black), a courier dot rides a route to a pin, the pin becomes the brand mark, and the wordmark wipes out from behind it with "made with" above and the product name below.
</structure>

<build>
1. One HTML file, 1920x1080. Every style is computed from time inside seek(t): no CSS transitions, no timers, no state between frames.
2. The camera is one transform on a container, keyed [time, zoom, x, y] with eased segments and zoom interpolated in log space.
3. Springs are closed-form step responses for every pop and settle.
4. Every handoff between layers is a shared element: the lime flood carries a copy of the bubble's words, the button carries its own label into the page.
5. Sound: a downloaded SFX for every event (Mixkit): typing, the send pop, a pop per toss, an impact on the drop, a swoosh for the cards, a click, a success tone, a whoosh as the button fills the page, a sparkle on the mark. Place each by its measured peak and loudnorm to -14 LUFS.
6. Render with Playwright: 8 subframes per frame blended with ffmpeg tmix, 60fps. Then step through every fast moment frame by frame and scan the whole video for single-frame pops.
</build>

<gotchas>
4 subframes leave ghost copies on fast moves, so use 8 and slow the move down. A flood must clear the farthest corner and take about 0.35s, or it reads as a flash. Set z-index on every layer, or the card floats over the flood. Never let the camera chase a wrapping text cursor: fixed lines only. Declare every variable before the first seek() runs.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for the inputs, then show me the beat map and 4 stills (ask, drop, chat, outro) before you write the full film.
</start>

Use Blender MCP to refine an existing rigged boar animation against a side-view video reference (144 frames at 24 fps, 6 seconds).

First inspect the scene, rig, rest pose, bone hierarchy, mesh weights, and existing animation. Create a verified backup before making changes.

Set up a synchronized side-by-side comparison in Blender: reference on the left, model on the right, with matching frame numbers. Review all 144 frames and match the visible motion as closely as the model’s proportions allow. Explicitly identify any poses inferred because of occlusion or missing depth information.

Animate complete leg chains from the shoulders and hips, with appropriate body movement and weight transfer. Preserve bone lengths. Match footfall timing, hoof placement and orientation, swing height, stride length, and joint bending. Avoid excessive bending of supporting legs, ground penetration, foot sliding, and unnatural hoof tilt.

Validate the front and hind legs separately before smoothing. Previous attempts improved the front legs but left the hind legs with short strides, insufficient swing flexion, and trajectories poorly positioned relative to the pelvis. Smoothing preserved these errors instead of correcting them.

Once the gait is correct, improve continuity without changing footfall timing or ground contact. Check interpolated and subframe poses using the deformed hoof mesh, not only bone positions. Treat numerical smoothness and contact checks as supporting evidence; also inspect the rendered motion.

If working from v4, preserve the approved front legs, torso, head, and tail animation, and modify only the hind-leg chains. Use the reference to determine hind-leg timing; do not assume a fixed offset from the front legs.

Deliver the updated .blend file and synchronized comparison video. Briefly report what changed, what failed and how it was fixed, what was verified, and any remaining mismatch. Do not claim an exact 1:1 match unless the comparison supports it.
